notes: Reasoning Ability topic package 4 for BATCH_010: 50 original questions on ranking, input-output, data sufficiency, assumptions, conclusions, cause and effect and critical reasoning, built by tools/packages/REAS_pkg4.py. Ranking positions and input-output machines are recomputed in code, comparison puzzles brute-forced for a unique order, and data sufficiency checked by enumerating models for each statement subset. Verbal items are hand-written and were re-answered blind by separate fresh solvers. All questions await human review.

stimuli.title: A row of unknown length
stimuli.content:
Some persons sit in a row, all facing north.

- Arun is 8th from the left end.
- Bela sits to the right of Arun, and exactly five persons sit between Arun and Bela.
- Chetan sits third to the left of Bela.
- Exactly four persons sit between Chetan and Dinesh, and Dinesh sits to the right of Bela.
- Dinesh is 4th from the right end of the row.
stimuli.solution: From the left: Arun 8th, Bela 8 + 6 = 14th, Chetan 14 − 3 = 11th. Dinesh is five places from Chetan (6th or 16th) and to the right of Bela, so 16th; being 4th from the right, the row has 16 + 4 − 1 = 19 persons.

stimuli.title: Machine: second letters to the right
stimuli.content:
A word arrangement machine rearranges a line of words step by step. In each step it takes, among the words not yet arranged, the word whose SECOND letter comes earliest in the alphabet, and places it at the right end, immediately to the left of the words already arranged there (in Step I, at the extreme right). The other words keep their order. A step that would not change the line is not counted, and the machine stops when the arrangement is complete.

Input: drum flute horn piano tabla veena guitar
stimuli.solution:
Second letters: drum r, flute l, horn o, piano i, tabla a, veena e, guitar u. Order of selection: tabla, veena, piano, flute, horn, drum, guitar.

Step I: drum flute horn piano veena guitar tabla
Step II: drum flute horn piano guitar veena tabla
Step III: drum flute horn guitar piano veena tabla
Step IV: drum horn guitar flute piano veena tabla
Step V: drum guitar horn flute piano veena tabla
Step VI: guitar drum horn flute piano veena tabla

stimuli.title: Machine: halve or add three, then rotate
stimuli.content:
A number machine changes a line of numbers step by step. In each step it first replaces every number: an odd number by that number plus 3, and an even number by half of it. It then moves the number at the left end of the line to the right end; the other numbers keep their order. The machine runs for four steps.

Input: 36 15 48 27 64 9

stimuli.title: Machine: words and numbers in turn
stimuli.content:
A word and number arrangement machine rearranges a line step by step, moving one element per step. In Steps I, III, V, … it takes, among the words not yet arranged, the word that comes last in alphabetical order and places it at the left end, immediately to the right of the words already placed there. In Steps II, IV, VI, … it takes the smallest number not yet arranged, reverses its digits, and places the result at the right end, immediately to the left of the numbers already placed there. All other elements keep their order. The machine stops when every element has been arranged.

Input: 81 lime jade 52 mint 37 rose 46
stimuli.solution:
Words in order: rose, mint, lime, jade. Numbers in order: 37 → 73, 46 → 64, 52 → 25, 81 → 18.

Step I: rose 81 lime jade 52 mint 37 46
Step II: rose 81 lime jade 52 mint 46 73
Step III: rose mint 81 lime jade 52 46 73
Step IV: rose mint 81 lime jade 52 64 73
Step V: rose mint lime 81 jade 52 64 73
Step VI: rose mint lime 81 jade 25 64 73
Step VII: rose mint lime jade 81 25 64 73
Step VIII: rose mint lime jade 18 25 64 73

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Twenty-six children sit in a row facing north. Tia is 12th from the right end. How many children sit to the left of Tia?

solution.concept: Children to the left = position from the left − 1
solution.explanation: Tia is 26 − 12 + 1 = 15th from the left, so 14 children sit to her left.
steps: Tia = 26 − 12 + 1 = 15th from the left
To her left: 15 − 1 = 14
solution.why_others_wrong: Fifteen is her position from the left; Eleven counts the children to her right; Thirteen subtracts one too many.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Fourteen

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Five students Arya, Bela, Chhavi, Dina and Esha scored different marks in a test.
- Arya scored more than Bela but less than Chhavi.
- Dina scored less than Bela.
- Esha scored more than Chhavi.

Who scored the lowest marks?

solution.concept: Join the comparisons
solution.explanation: Esha > Chhavi > Arya > Bela > Dina. Dina scored the lowest.
steps: Chhavi > Arya > Bela
Bela > Dina
Esha > Chhavi
solution.why_others_wrong: Bela is second lowest, Arya in the middle and Esha the highest.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Dina

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Five boxes P, Q, R, S and T have different weights.
- Box Q is heavier than only box R.
- Box S is lighter than only box T.

Which box is exactly in the middle when the boxes are arranged by weight?

solution.concept: 'Heavier than only one' = second lightest
solution.explanation: Q is heavier than R alone, so R is the lightest and Q second lightest. S is lighter than T alone, so T is the heaviest and S second heaviest. P is left for the middle place.
steps: R lightest, Q 2nd lightest
T heaviest, S 2nd heaviest
Middle: P
solution.why_others_wrong: Q and S are the second lightest and second heaviest; R is the lightest.
solution.final_answer: Option D: P

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Twenty-five students with roll numbers 1 to 25 sit in a row facing north, in order of roll number from the left end. All the students with odd roll numbers leave the row, and the others do not move relative to one another. What is the position of roll number 14 from the right end in the new row?

solution.concept: Count only the students who remain
solution.explanation: The remaining students are roll numbers 2, 4, …, 24 — twelve students. Roll number 14 is 7th of them from the left, so it is 12 − 7 + 1 = 6th from the right.
steps: Remaining: 2, 4, …, 24 (12 students)
14 is 7th from the left
From the right: 12 − 7 + 1 = 6th
solution.why_others_wrong: 7th is its place from the left; 12th is the number of students left; 5th forgets the + 1.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 6th

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Eighteen lamp posts stand in a straight row, 25 m apart from one another. What is the distance between the 3rd post from the left end and the 4th post from the right end?

solution.concept: Distance = number of gaps × gap length
solution.explanation: The 4th post from the right is 18 − 4 + 1 = 15th from the left. From the 3rd to the 15th post there are 15 − 3 = 12 gaps of 25 m: 300 m.
steps: 4th from right = 15th from left
solution.why_others_wrong: 325 m counts 13 gaps (posts, not spaces); 275 m counts 11; 350 m counts 14.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 300 m

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many persons sit in the row?

solution.concept: Place everyone from the left end first
solution.explanation: Arun 8th, Bela 14th, Chetan 11th, Dinesh 16th from the left; Dinesh is 4th from the right, so the row has 16 + 4 − 1 = 19 persons.
steps: Arun 8, Bela 14, Chetan 11, Dinesh 16
solution.why_others_wrong: 18 and 20 drop or double the − 1; 22 places Dinesh on the wrong side of Chetan.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 19

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many persons sit between Arun and Dinesh?

solution.concept: Between = gap − 1
solution.explanation: Arun is 8th and Dinesh 16th from the left: 16 − 8 − 1 = 7 persons sit between them.
solution.why_others_wrong: Eight forgets the − 1; Six subtracts one too many; Nine counts both ends.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Seven

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: What is Chetan's position from the right end?

solution.concept: Position from the other end = total − position + 1
solution.explanation: Chetan is 11th from the left in a row of 19: 19 − 11 + 1 = 9th from the right.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11th is his place from the left; 8th and 10th misuse the + 1.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 9th

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Esha sits exactly midway between Arun and Dinesh. Who sits immediately to the left of Esha?

solution.concept: Midway = average of the two positions
solution.explanation: Arun is 8th and Dinesh 16th, so Esha is (8 + 16) ÷ 2 = 12th from the left. The 11th place, immediately to her left, is Chetan's.
steps: 11th = Chetan
solution.why_others_wrong: Bela is two places to Esha's right; Arun and Dinesh are the two ends of the stretch.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Chetan

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
A word and number arrangement machine rearranges a line step by step. In each step it makes two moves: (1) among the numbers not yet arranged, it takes the one that leaves the smallest remainder when divided by 7, replaces it by the quotient of that division, and places the quotient at the left end, immediately to the right of the quotients already placed there; (2) among the words not yet arranged, it takes the one that comes last in alphabetical order, writes it in capital letters, and places it at the right end, immediately to the left of the words already placed there. All other elements keep their order.

Input: pearl 45 coral 30 amber 61 topaz 20

What is the sum of all the numbers in Step III?

solution.concept: Track which numbers are still unchanged in the step
solution.explanation: Remainders on division by 7: 30 → 2, 45 → 3, 61 → 5, 20 → 6, so the numbers are taken in the order 30, 45, 61, 20 and become 4, 6, 8, 2. Words from last alphabetically: topaz, pearl, coral, amber. Step I: 4 pearl 45 coral amber 61 20 TOPAZ. Step II: 4 6 coral amber 61 20 PEARL TOPAZ. Step III: 4 6 8 amber 20 CORAL PEARL TOPAZ. Sum of the numbers in Step III = 38.
steps: Step I: 4 pearl 45 coral amber 61 20 TOPAZ
Step II: 4 6 coral amber 61 20 PEARL TOPAZ
Step III: 4 6 8 amber 20 CORAL PEARL TOPAZ
solution.final_answer: Option B: 38

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: Notice in a public park: "Keep the park clean. Use the dustbins."

Assumptions:
I. There are dustbins in the park.
II. Some visitors may litter the park if they are not reminded.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: Visitors are told to use the dustbins, so the notice takes for granted that dustbins are there (I). A reminder to keep the park clean is put up only if littering is expected otherwise (II).
steps: Instruction to use dustbins ⇒ dustbins exist: I
Reminder ⇒ littering is possible: II
solution.why_others_wrong: Each 'Only' option drops one of two things the notice rests on.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Both I and II are implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: Railway announcement: "Book your tickets early — seats fill up fast during the holidays."

Assumptions:
I. Many people travel by train during the holidays.
II. Train fares are lower during the holidays.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: Seats fill up fast only if many people travel then (I). The announcement says nothing about fares, so II is not implicit.
steps: Seats fill fast ⇒ heavy holiday travel: I
Fares not mentioned ⇒ II not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both accept a claim about fares; Neither ignores the reason given for booking early.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only assumption I is implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: Advertisement: "Wanted: a driver who can also speak English, for a travel company."

Assumptions:
I. Every driver in the city speaks English.
II. Some drivers are able to speak English.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: The company asks for an English-speaking driver because it expects some drivers to have that skill (II). If every driver spoke English, there would be no need to mention it, so I is not assumed.
steps: Asking for a skill ⇒ some candidates have it: II
Mentioning it ⇒ not everyone has it ⇒ I not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Only I and Both accept a claim that would make the requirement pointless; Neither misses the basis of the advertisement.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Only assumption II is implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: Notice from a school: "The school will remain closed on Monday on account of the local festival."

Assumptions:
I. Every student of the school celebrates the festival.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit

steps: 'Every student' is an extreme claim ⇒ I not implicit
Only Monday is mentioned ⇒ II not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Each other option accepts a claim that the notice does not depend on.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Neither I nor II is implicit

Purpose of a poster ⇒ people may act on it: II

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: "Every employee will get a bonus of one month's salary if the company's profit this year crosses ₹100 crore," announced the company's chief executive.

Assumptions:
I. It is possible for the company's profit to cross ₹100 crore this year.
II. Employees will not work at all unless they are promised a bonus.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: A conditional bonus is announced only if the condition can be met (I). The offer may be meant to encourage employees, but it does not assume that they would stop working altogether without it (II is extreme).
steps: Promise tied to a target ⇒ the target is reachable: I
'Not work at all' is an extreme claim ⇒ II not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both accept an extreme claim; Neither ignores that the target must be reachable.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only assumption I is implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: A bank has cut its home-loan interest rate by 0.25 percentage point to attract new borrowers.

Assumptions:
I. Some borrowers choose a lender partly on the basis of the interest rate it charges.
II. Other banks will not cut their home-loan rates.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: A rate cut can attract borrowers only if borrowers care about the rate (I). The bank may expect rivals to follow; its move does not depend on their keeping their rates unchanged (II).
steps: Rate cut to attract borrowers ⇒ borrowers compare rates: I
Rivals' reaction is not part of the plan ⇒ II not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both assume something about other banks that the decision does not need; Neither ignores why a rate cut would attract anyone.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only assumption I is implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: Order of the district collector: "In view of the heavy-rain forecast for tomorrow, all schools in the district will remain closed tomorrow."

Assumptions:
I. The forecast of heavy rain for tomorrow will certainly come true.
II. Heavy rain could make it unsafe for children to travel to and from school.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.explanation: Schools are closed because heavy rain could endanger children on their way (II). Acting on a forecast as a precaution does not require being certain that it will come true, so I ('certainly') is not assumed.
steps: Closure for safety ⇒ rain can make travel unsafe: II
Precaution, not certainty ⇒ I not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Only I and Both treat a precaution as a certainty; Neither misses the safety reason for the closure.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Only assumption II is implicit

questions.question_text:

Assumptions:
I. Every girl in the state already owns a bicycle.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: Notice from a company: "Employees may work from home on Fridays, provided their work does not suffer."

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit

solution.explanation: Allowing work from home makes sense only if at least some work can be done from home (II). The notice allows work on Fridays, from home; it does not assume that all the week's work is done by Thursday (I).

Friday is still a working day ⇒ I not implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: Each of the five trainees in a batch passed at least one of two tests, Hindi and English. Exactly three of them passed the Hindi test, and exactly three passed the English test.

Conclusions:
I. At least one trainee passed both tests.
II. Exactly one trainee passed both tests.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: Passing counts add up to 3 + 3 = 6 for 5 trainees who each passed at least one test, so exactly 6 − 5 = 1 trainee was counted twice, that is, passed both. 'Exactly one' (II) and therefore 'at least one' (I) both follow.
steps: 3 + 3 − both = 5 ⇒ both = 1
⇒ II, and hence I
solution.why_others_wrong: Each 'Only' option drops one of two consequences of the same count.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: A clock gains exactly 5 minutes every hour. It was set to the correct time at 8:00 am today.

Conclusions:
I. When the correct time is 12:00 noon today, the clock shows 12:20 pm.
II. The clock will show the correct time again later today.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: In 4 hours the clock gains 4 × 5 = 20 minutes, so at noon it shows 12:20 pm (I). To show the correct time again it must gain a full 12 hours (720 minutes), which takes 720 ÷ 5 = 144 hours — not today (II is false).
steps: Gain by noon: 4 × 5 = 20 min ⇒ I
Gain needed: 720 min ⇒ 144 hours ⇒ II false
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both accept a conclusion the rate rules out; Neither ignores the direct calculation.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only conclusion I follows

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: Bina is the only sister of Ankit's father.

Conclusions:
I. Bina is Ankit's aunt.
II. Ankit's father has no brother.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: The sister of one's father is one's aunt, so I follows. Being the only sister means Ankit's father has no other sister; it says nothing about brothers, so II does not follow.
steps: Father's sister = aunt ⇒ I
'Only sister' says nothing about brothers ⇒ II does not follow
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both read 'only sister' as 'only sibling'; Neither misses the direct relation.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only conclusion I follows

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: The company's revenue this year was the highest in its history.

Conclusions:
I. The company made a profit this year.
II. The company's revenue will be higher next year.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: Revenue is what the company earned from sales; profit also depends on its costs, which are not given, so I does not follow. A record this year says nothing certain about next year, so II does not follow.
steps: Revenue ≠ profit ⇒ I does not follow
No information about next year ⇒ II does not follow
solution.why_others_wrong: Each other option treats record revenue as if it guaranteed profit or future growth.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: A club has 60 members. 25 of them play tennis, and every member who plays tennis also swims. 20 members neither play tennis nor swim.

Conclusions:
I. More members of the club play tennis than swim.
II. Exactly 15 members of the club swim but do not play tennis.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: The 40 members who do something all swim (tennis players swim too, and the rest of the 40 must swim). So 40 swim, of whom 25 also play tennis: 40 − 25 = 15 swim without playing tennis (II). Since 40 swim and 25 play tennis, I is false.
steps: Swimmers = 60 − 20 = 40
Swim only = 40 − 25 = 15 ⇒ II
40 > 25 ⇒ I false
solution.why_others_wrong: Only I and Both reverse the comparison; Neither ignores the direct count.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Only conclusion II follows

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: The bus fare from a village to the town is ₹30 per passenger. An auto-rickshaw makes the same trip for ₹90, whether it carries one, two or three passengers.

Conclusions:
I. For three people travelling together, the auto-rickshaw costs the same as the bus.
II. For two people travelling together, the bus is cheaper than the auto-rickshaw.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: Three people pay 3 × ₹30 = ₹90 by bus, the same as the auto-rickshaw (I). Two people pay ₹60 by bus, less than ₹90 (II).
solution.why_others_wrong: Each 'Only' option drops one of two direct comparisons.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: Some of the bank's branches open on Sundays. Every branch of the bank that opens on Sundays has a cash-deposit machine.

Conclusions:
I. Some of the bank's branches that have a cash-deposit machine open on Sundays.
II. Every branch of the bank that has a cash-deposit machine opens on Sundays.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: The branches that open on Sundays exist and all have cash-deposit machines, so some branches with machines open on Sundays (I). 'Every Sunday branch has a machine' cannot be reversed: branches with machines may also be closed on Sundays, so II does not follow.
steps: Some branches open on Sundays; all of them have machines ⇒ I
Converse of an 'every' statement ⇒ II does not follow
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both reverse the 'every' statement; Neither misses the 'some' conclusion.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only conclusion I follows

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Claim: Keeping the school library open during the lunch break will increase the number of books that students borrow.

Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the claim?

options.text: The library has more than 5,000 books
At present the library is open only during class hours, when most students cannot visit it
Some students bring their own books to school

solution.concept: Strengthen: show that access is the obstacle now
solution.explanation: If students borrow few books because the library is open only when they are in class, opening it at lunch removes that obstacle, so more books are likely to be borrowed.
steps: Claim: more opening time ⇒ more borrowing
Strengthener: students cannot visit at present
solution.why_others_wrong: The size of the collection and the length of the break do not show that students will come; students with their own books are, if anything, less likely to borrow.
solution.final_answer: Option C: At present the library is open only during class hours, when most students cannot visit it

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: A recipe that serves 4 people needs 300 g of rice. Neha is making the same recipe for 10 people, using rice in the same proportion.

Which of the following can be inferred?

solution.concept: Scale in proportion to the number of people
solution.explanation: Rice per person = 300 ÷ 4 = 75 g, so 10 people need 75 × 10 = 750 g.
steps: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 g per person
solution.why_others_wrong: 600 g doubles the recipe; 1,200 g quadruples it; 3 kg multiplies by ten instead of by 10 ÷ 4.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Neha needs 750 g of rice

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: Several elderly residents of a housing society have slipped and fallen on the society's staircase, whose steps are worn smooth and have no handrail.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Ask the elderly residents to stay indoors
Stop visitors from using the staircase
Fit handrails and anti-slip strips on the staircase

solution.concept: Remove the cause of the falls
solution.explanation: The falls are caused by smooth steps with nothing to hold. Handrails and anti-slip strips fix both causes.
steps: Cause: smooth steps, no handrail
Remedy: anti-slip strips + handrails
solution.why_others_wrong: Keeping residents indoors or closing the staircase is impractical; stopping visitors does not make the steps safer.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Fit handrails and anti-slip strips on the staircase

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Claim: A café's new menu is popular with its customers, because the café's sales rose by 40% in the first week after the new menu was introduced.

Which of the following, if true, most weakens the claim?

options.text: The new menu has more vegetarian dishes than the old one
The café is located near a college
During that first week, the café gave a 50% discount on every item to celebrate the new menu
The café's owner designed the new menu herself

solution.concept: Weaken: give another reason for the rise
solution.explanation: A half-price offer in the same week could explain the jump in sales by itself, so the rise does not show that customers like the new menu.
steps: Evidence: sales up 40% in week 1
Weakener: 50% discount in the same week
solution.why_others_wrong: The kind of dishes, the location and who designed the menu do not explain a sudden one-week rise.
solution.final_answer: Option C: During that first week, the café gave a 50% discount on every item to celebrate the new menu

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: Many small traders in a town are losing sales because they accept only cash, while more and more customers want to pay digitally.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Ban digital payments in the town
Ask customers to carry more cash
Help the traders open free QR-code payment accounts with their banks and show them how to use them
Close the shops that accept only cash

solution.concept: Enable the traders rather than restrict the customers
solution.explanation: Traders lose sales because they cannot accept digital payments. Helping them start accepting such payments removes the problem.
steps: Problem: cash-only traders lose customers
Remedy: enable digital payments
solution.why_others_wrong: Banning digital payments or telling customers to carry cash goes against what customers want; closing shops punishes the traders.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Help the traders open free QR-code payment accounts with their banks and show them how to use them

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: A museum gives free entry to children under 12 years of age and to people over 60. All other visitors pay ₹50 each. On Sunday, a family visited the museum: a grandmother aged 65, two parents aged 38 and 36, and two children aged 12 and 8.

Which of the following can be inferred?

options.text: The family paid ₹100 in all for entry
The family paid ₹200 in all for entry
The family paid ₹250 in all for entry
The family paid ₹150 in all for entry

solution.concept: Apply each condition exactly
solution.explanation: The grandmother (over 60) and the 8-year-old (under 12) enter free. The two parents and the 12-year-old (who is not under 12) pay ₹50 each: ₹150.
steps: Free: 65-year-old, 8-year-old
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹100 treats the 12-year-old as under 12; ₹200 charges the grandmother or the younger child; ₹250 charges everyone.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The family paid ₹150 in all for entry

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: Countries with more mobile phones per person have higher average incomes. So giving free mobile phones to families in the state's poorest districts will raise their incomes.

Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

options.text: A trial last year that gave free phones to 10,000 families in two of the poorest districts found no change in their incomes after a year, compared with similar families who did not get phones
Mobile phones have become cheaper in recent years
Most people in the poorest districts work in farming
Several companies sell mobile phones in the state

solution.concept: Weaken: direct evidence against the predicted effect
solution.explanation: The argument predicts that free phones will raise incomes. A controlled trial in the same kind of districts found no effect, which directly undercuts the prediction drawn from a country-level link.
steps: Prediction: free phones ⇒ higher incomes
Weakener: trial shows no effect
solution.why_others_wrong: Cheaper phones, the main occupation and the number of sellers do not show whether phones raise incomes.
solution.final_answer: Option A: A trial last year that gave free phones to 10,000 families in two of the poorest districts found no change in their incomes after a year, compared with similar families who did not get phones

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: The hospital's new rule that doctors must wash their hands before examining each patient is the reason infections among its patients fell by 30% this year.

Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

options.text: The hospital made no other change this year in its cleaning, staffing or kinds of patients, and similar hospitals without the rule saw no fall in infections
Hand-washing takes doctors less than a minute
Doctors at the hospital agreed with the new rule

solution.concept: Strengthen: rule out other explanations
solution.explanation: If nothing else changed at the hospital and comparable hospitals without the rule saw no fall, the new rule is the most likely reason for the drop in infections.
steps: Claim: rule ⇒ fewer infections
Strengthener: no other change; no fall elsewhere
solution.why_others_wrong: The time hand-washing takes, the hospital's size and doctors' agreement do not link the rule to the fall.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The hospital made no other change this year in its cleaning, staffing or kinds of patients, and similar hospitals without the rule saw no fall in infections

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: Five lectures — on Economics, History, Law, Maths and Physics — are held one after another on a day. Law is held immediately after History. Maths is the third lecture. Physics is held at some time before Economics.

Which of the following must be true?

options.text: Physics is held immediately before Economics

solution.concept: Find every arrangement, then pick what holds in all
solution.explanation: History–Law must take places 1–2 or 4–5 (Maths is 3rd). If they are 1–2, Physics and Economics are 4th and 5th; if they are 4–5, Physics and Economics are 1st and 2nd. In both cases Physics comes immediately before Economics.
steps: Case 1: History, Law, Maths, Physics, Economics
Case 2: Physics, Economics, Maths, History, Law
Common to both: Physics just before Economics
solution.why_others_wrong: Each of the other options holds in only one of the two possible orders.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Physics is held immediately before Economics

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: A survey found that the city's buses run almost empty between 11 am and 4 pm but are badly overcrowded during the morning and evening peak hours.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Stop all bus services between 11 am and 4 pm
Buy enough new buses to double the fleet at once
Raise fares sharply during peak hours to keep people off the buses
Shift some buses from the afternoon schedule to the peak hours, and offer lower fares in the afternoon

solution.concept: Match supply to demand at low cost
solution.explanation: Buses are idle in the afternoon and short at peak hours. Moving buses to the peak hours uses the existing fleet better, and cheaper afternoon fares can draw some travellers away from the peaks.
steps: Problem: mismatch between bus supply and demand
Remedy: reschedule buses + off-peak fares
solution.why_others_wrong: Stopping afternoon buses strands those who travel then; doubling the fleet is costly and leaves more empty buses; sharp peak fares penalise people who must travel at those hours.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Shift some buses from the afternoon schedule to the peak hours, and offer lower fares in the afternoon

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: Patients who choose Dr Mehta for knee surgery recover faster than the patients of the other knee surgeons at the hospital. So Dr Mehta is the hospital's best knee surgeon.

Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

options.text: Dr Mehta has worked at the hospital for ten years
The hospital has four knee surgeons
Dr Mehta's patients pay the same fees as other patients
Dr Mehta operates mostly on young athletes with minor injuries, while the other surgeons treat most of the elderly patients with severe knee damage

solution.concept: Weaken: the groups being compared differ
solution.explanation: Young patients with minor injuries recover faster whoever operates on them. If Dr Mehta's patients are mostly such cases, their faster recovery does not show that he is the best surgeon.
steps: Evidence: faster recovery of Dr Mehta's patients
Weakener: his patients are easier cases
solution.why_others_wrong: Years of service, the number of surgeons and fees do not explain the difference in recovery.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Dr Mehta operates mostly on young athletes with minor injuries, while the other surgeons treat most of the elderly patients with severe knee damage

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: In a class, the average mark of the 20 boys is 60, and the average mark of the 30 girls is 70. There are no other students in the class.

Which of the following must be true?

options.text: The average mark of the whole class is 66
The average mark of the whole class is 65
At least one girl scored more than 70
Every girl scored more than every boy

solution.concept: A combined average is weighted by group size
solution.explanation: Total marks = 20 × 60 + 30 × 70 = 1,200 + 2,100 = 3,300 for 50 students: average 66.
solution.why_others_wrong: 65 averages the two averages without weighting; every girl could have scored exactly 70; averages say nothing about every individual.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The average mark of the whole class is 66

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: An audit found that the city's government hospitals often run out of essential medicines because each hospital places its own orders late and in small quantities.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Stop giving free medicines at the hospitals
Ask patients to bring their own medicines
Set up a central system that tracks every hospital's stock and places orders automatically before stocks run low
Order a five-year stock of every medicine at once

solution.concept: Fix the ordering process that causes the shortage
solution.explanation: Shortages come from late, small orders by each hospital. Central tracking with automatic reordering keeps stocks up without the waste of huge one-time purchases.
steps: Cause: late, small orders
Remedy: central tracking + automatic reordering
solution.why_others_wrong: Stopping free medicines or shifting the burden to patients defeats the purpose of the hospitals; a five-year stock would expire and waste money.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Set up a central system that tracks every hospital's stock and places orders automatically before stocks run low
